log.content:
The problem defines the sequence $\{a_n\}$ recursively. First, I calculated the initial terms:
$a_1 = 0$
$a_2 = 1$
$a_3 = 2$
$a_4 = 4$
$a_5 = 5$
$a_6 = 7$
$a_7 = 9$
$a_8 = 12$
$a_9 = 13$
$a_{10} = 15$

By analyzing the recurrence $a_n = \max_{1 \le i \le n-1} \{a_i + a_{n-i} + \min(i, n-i)\}$, we observed that the maximum is consistently achieved when $i = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$. This simplifies the recurrence to:
$$
a_n = \begin{cases} 2a_{n/2} + n/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is even} \\ a_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} + a_{\lceil n/2 \rceil} + \lfloor n/2 \rfloor & \text{if } n \text{ is odd} \end{cases}
$$
I used this simplified recurrence to calculate $a_{2025}$ recursively, performing intermediate calculations manually and verifying the final result with Python code.

The recursive substitution led to:
$a_{2025} = 23 a_{63} + 9 a_{64} + 5053$.
Substituting further led to $a_{2025} = 23 a_{15} + 105 a_{16} + 7055$.
Using $a_{15} = 28$ and $a_{16} = 32$, we found $a_{2025} = 644 + 3360 + 7055 = 11059$.

I will now use the code tool to confirm this result.

The recurrence relation simplifies to $a_n = a_{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} + a_{\lceil n/2 \rceil} + \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ for odd $n$, and $a_n = 2a_{n/2} + n/2$ for even $n$. By applying this recurrence relation recursively, I computed $a_{2025}$. The calculation confirmed that $a_{2025} = 11059$.

Final Answer: 11059.
